title: Authentication and tenant isolation before shared deployment
body:
HermesMQ is feature-complete against the architecture, but every endpoint is wide open: anyone who can reach the port can create or delete topics, publish, and read any subscription's backlog. Before it can run anywhere shared it needs authentication (who is calling) and tenant isolation (callers only see their own topics and subscriptions).

Every REST and gRPC request authenticates from a bearer token or API key; keys are configured as salted hashes and resolve to a Principal(tenantId, scopes). Tenants are isolated by transparently namespacing resource ids at the API boundary, so cross-tenant access is impossible by construction. Admin operations require an admin scope. /health and /metrics stay unauthenticated for probes and scraping. Configurable and fail-fast, with an auth-disabled default-tenant mode for local dev and backward compatibility with existing single-tenant journals.
